# server

self-host Coder: the server, its dashboard and sign-in

Self-host Coder: the server your agents and platform apps talk to, with a dashboard and sign-in. We run one as the hosted service; you can run your own.

## `server serve [--port <port>] [--host <host>] [--memory] [--runner <runner>] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

run the server

Run the Coder server on Bun: the address platforms deliver events to, the dashboard, and the worker that runs tasks. With DATABASE_URL it is a full server with sign-in and workspaces. Without one it is the dashboard for this machine's CLI: its config, agents, tasks and engine logins, on loopback only. --memory makes a throwaway test server that keeps everything in memory. Configured through the environment; every variable is in coder docs self-host.

- `--port <port>` listen port (default: PORT, else the port in a localhost PUBLIC_URL, else 8787)
- `--host <host>` listen address (default: HOST, else 127.0.0.1 without a database, else every interface)
- `--memory` a throwaway test server: everything in memory, no sign-in, admin token only
- `--runner <runner>` local, local-docker, vercel-sandbox, github-actions, or http
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

Environment:

- `PUBLIC_URL` the address platforms and browsers reach the server at (default http://localhost:<port>)
- `PORT` listen port, as hosts set it (default 8787)
- `HOST` listen address, as --host
- `DATABASE_URL` Postgres, set up with drizzle-kit push; turns on sign-in and workspaces
- `AUTH_WULAR_URL` the Wular Auth issuer people sign in with (default https://auth.wular.ai)
- `SERVER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` encrypts stored secrets and derives the sign-in keys; required with DATABASE_URL (openssl rand -base64 32)
- `RUNNER` where tasks run: local (default), local-docker, vercel-sandbox, github-actions, http
- `MAX_TASKS, TASK_TIMEOUT, TASK_STALL, TASK_ATTEMPTS` runner capacity and lifecycle limits
- `ADMIN_TOKEN` local and memory servers: the dashboard and CLI key; minted and shown when unset
- `CODER_CACHE_HOME` archived tasks, flows and usage (default OS cache directory/wular-coder)
- `WORK_DIR` where the local runner keeps task work folders
- `SERVER_NAME` what the dashboard calls this server (default Coder)

```sh
PUBLIC_URL=https://abc.ngrok.app coder server serve  # receive GitHub and Slack events through a tunnel; the tunnel serves only their webhooks and callbacks
PUBLIC_URL=https://agents.example.com DATABASE_URL=postgres://... coder server serve  # on your own host, backed by Postgres
```

## `server rotate-key [--json]`

re-seal secrets with SERVER_ENCRYPTION_KEY

Re-seal stored app, installation, engine, and linked user secrets with the current key.

- `--json` JSON output

Environment:

- `SERVER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` the new key
- `SERVER_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS` the old key, still accepted while rotating

## `server workflow`

print the GitHub Actions workflow for RUNNER=github-actions

Print the workflow the github-actions runner dispatches. Save it as .github/workflows/coder-agent.yml in every repo the agent runs on, and set RUNNER=github-actions on the server.

```sh
coder server workflow > .github/workflows/coder-agent.yml  # add it to a repo
```

## server app

the built-in agent's public apps

The built-in agent's apps, one per platform, shared by every workspace on this server.

## `server app create <integration> [--org <org>] [--name <name>] [--json]`

create the built-in agent's public app

Open the page that creates the built-in agent's public app on a platform, once per server. Every workspace then connects it from its dashboard with one click. Run it where the server's environment is set.

- `<integration>` the platform, such as github
- `--org <org>` create it under this organization instead of your own account
- `--name <name>` the app's name and handle (default Coder)
- `--json` JSON output

Environment:

- `DATABASE_URL` the server's Postgres
- `PUBLIC_URL` the server's address, which goes into the app

```sh
coder server app create github --name wular-coder  # the hosted GitHub App
```
